# greeting-strcpy

`greet(out, cap, name)` behaves exactly like `snprintf(out, cap, "Hello, %s!", name)`: it never writes more than `cap` bytes, truncates, always terminates, and returns the untruncated length (11 for `Ann`). `cap == 0` writes nothing and `out` may be NULL. Build and tests run under AddressSanitizer.

prompt: Security ticket for the kiosk greeter (CWE-120). Problem: `greet` builds the greeting with `strcpy`/`strcat` and ignores the capacity it was given, so a long name (names come from a badge scanner) overflows the caller's buffer on the heap. Acceptance: hostile input can no longer do this, every documented behaviour still works, and the fix is in the code (not in the tests). Don't weaken the visible tests.
verify: mkdir -p build && gcc -std=c11 -O1 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -Wall -Wextra -Iinclude -Isrc -o build/tests $(find src tests -name '*.c') && ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0:allocator_may_return_null=1 UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1:print_stacktrace=0 ./build/tests

start.README.md:
# log-format-string

`log_line(out, cap, text)` copies the text byte for byte (truncated to `cap - 1` characters, always NUL-terminated) and returns the number of characters stored. Texts such as `100%`, `%s%s%s`, `%n%n` and `%x %x` come out unchanged.

prompt: log_line is unsafe: `log_line` passes the user's text to `snprintf` as the *format string*: a message such as `%s%s%s%s` reads garbage from the stack (crash or leak), `%n` writes to memory, and any `%` in a legitimate message is mangled. fix it without breaking normal use, README.md says what normal is.
verify: mkdir -p build && gcc -std=c11 -O1 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -Wall -Wextra -Iinclude -Isrc -o build/tests $(find src tests -name '*.c') && ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0:allocator_may_return_null=1 UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1:print_stacktrace=0 ./build/tests

start.README.md:
# prefix-fencepost

`sum_prefix(a, n, count)` sums exactly `min(count, n)` elements. `count == 0` and `n == 0` give 0 (and `a` may then be NULL).

prompt: Review comment on `sum_prefix`: `sum_prefix` loops with `i <= m` instead of `i < m`: it adds one element too many (wrong totals) and when the whole array is requested it reads one `int` past the end of the buffer. Please fix this properly and keep the existing functionality, including unusual but valid inputs. Nobody should be able to work around the fix with a variant of the payload.
verify: mkdir -p build && gcc -std=c11 -O1 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -Wall -Wextra -Iinclude -Isrc -o build/tests $(find src tests -name '*.c') && ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0:allocator_may_return_null=1 UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1:print_stacktrace=0 ./build/tests

start.README.md:
# score-index

`score_at(scores, n, index, out)` accepts exactly the indexes `0 .. n-1`. Everything else returns -1 without touching `*out`; `n == 0` accepts nothing.

prompt: We had an incident review for the leaderboard. Root cause: `score_at` only rejects indexes greater than `n` (so `n` itself is accepted) and never looks at negative indexes: `/scores/-1` and `/scores/5` on a five-element table read memory next to the array. Close the hole in `score_at` and anything that shares the flaw in this repository; normal users must notice nothing.
verify: mkdir -p build && gcc -std=c11 -O1 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -Wall -Wextra -Iinclude -Isrc -o build/tests $(find src tests -name '*.c') && ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0:allocator_may_return_null=1 UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1:print_stacktrace=0 ./build/tests

start.README.md:
# join-path-boundary

`join_path` follows the header comment: success when `len + 1 <= cap`, otherwise -1 with `out[0] = 0` (`cap == 0` writes nothing at all). The result for fitting inputs is unchanged.

prompt: Security ticket for the file browser (CWE-193). Problem: `join_path` compares the length of the result with the capacity but forgets the terminating NUL: when the joined path is exactly `cap` characters long, the NUL is written one byte past the end of the buffer. Acceptance: hostile input can no longer do this, every documented behaviour still works, and the fix is in the code (not in the tests). Don't weaken the visible tests.
verify: mkdir -p build && gcc -std=c11 -O1 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -Wall -Wextra -Iinclude -Isrc -o build/tests $(find src tests -name '*.c') && ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0:allocator_may_return_null=1 UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1:print_stacktrace=0 ./build/tests

start.README.md:
# config-line-parser

`parse_kv` honours `keycap` and `valcap` as described in the header: too-long keys or values are an error (-1, both buffers emptied), never a truncation, and nothing is ever written beyond the capacities.

prompt: parse_kv is unsafe: `parse_kv` copies the key and the value with `memcpy`/`strcpy` into the caller's buffers without looking at the capacities it receives, so a config line with a long key or value overflows the (fixed-size, often stack) buffers of the caller. fix it without breaking normal use, README.md says what normal is.
verify: mkdir -p build && gcc -std=c11 -O1 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -Wall -Wextra -Iinclude -Isrc -o build/tests $(find src tests -name '*.c') && ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0:allocator_may_return_null=1 UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1:print_stacktrace=0 ./build/tests

start.README.md:
# strncpy-terminator

`copy_field(dst, cap, src)` copies at most `cap - 1` characters and always writes the terminating NUL (for `cap > 0`). Sources that fit are copied unchanged; `cap == 0` writes nothing.

prompt: Our static analysis flagged `copy_field` (CWE-170): `copy_field` uses `strncpy(dst, src, cap)`, which does not terminate the destination when the source is `cap` characters or longer: every later `strlen`, `printf("%s")` or `strcpy` on the field runs off the end of the buffer. Harden the code. Existing behaviour for legitimate callers has to stay exactly as documented in README.md; there are tests for both the normal use and for hostile input.
verify: mkdir -p build && gcc -std=c11 -O1 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -Wall -Wextra -Iinclude -Isrc -o build/tests $(find src tests -name '*.c') && ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0:allocator_may_return_null=1 UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1:print_stacktrace=0 ./build/tests

start.README.md:
# word-splitter

`split_words` stores at most `max_words` pointers (extra words are ignored, `max_words == 0` stores nothing and returns 0); every stored word is still NUL-terminated in place. Words and separators behave as in the header comment.

prompt: A penetration test of the command-line parser reported a vulnerability: `split_words` stores a pointer for every word of the input and never checks `max_words`: a command line with more words than the caller's array has slots writes pointers past the end of that array. Fix it in the code so the whole class of problem is gone (not just the payload from the report) and keep everything legitimate working. README.md describes the intended behaviour.
verify: mkdir -p build && gcc -std=c11 -O1 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -Wall -Wextra -Iinclude -Isrc -o build/tests $(find src tests -name '*.c') && ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0:allocator_may_return_null=1 UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1:print_stacktrace=0 ./build/tests

start.README.md:
# repeat-allocation

`repeat_string` returns NULL (writing nothing) whenever `len * count + 1` would overflow `size_t` or `malloc` fails, and otherwise the repeated string exactly as before. Strings of length 0 and counts of 0 give an allocated empty string.

prompt: A penetration test of the banner generator reported a vulnerability: `repeat_string` computes the allocation size as `len * count + 1` without an overflow check: for `count = SIZE_MAX / 2 + 1` and a two-character string the product wraps to 0, `malloc(1)` succeeds, and the copy loop writes far beyond the one-byte block. Failed allocations are not checked either. Fix it in the code so the whole class of problem is gone (not just the payload from the report) and keep everything legitimate working. README.md describes the intended behaviour.
verify: mkdir -p build && gcc -std=c11 -O1 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -Wall -Wextra -Iinclude -Isrc -o build/tests $(find src tests -name '*.c') && ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0:allocator_may_return_null=1 UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1:print_stacktrace=0 ./build/tests

start.README.md:
# snprintf-accumulator

`join_items` returns the full length but never writes more than `cap` bytes, wherever the truncation happens (inside an item, inside a separator, or between items). The text produced for fitting buffers is unchanged.

prompt: Review comment on `join_items`: `join_items` adds the return value of `snprintf` (the length the output *would* have had) to its write position: as soon as one item does not fit, `used` exceeds `cap`, `cap - used` wraps to a huge number and the next `snprintf` writes to `out + used`, far outside the buffer. Please fix this properly and keep the existing functionality, including unusual but valid inputs. Nobody should be able to work around the fix with a variant of the payload.
verify: mkdir -p build && gcc -std=c11 -O1 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -Wall -Wextra -Iinclude -Isrc -o build/tests $(find src tests -name '*.c') && ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0:allocator_may_return_null=1 UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1:print_stacktrace=0 ./build/tests

start.README.md:
# string-builder-growth

`sb_append` grows the buffer until `len + n + 1` bytes fit (doubling, starting at 16), checks every size computation for overflow and every allocation for failure, and then behaves as before. On failure the builder is unchanged and still usable.

prompt: sb_append is unsafe: `sb_append` doubles the capacity once when the new text does not fit, but a single append can be much larger than the doubled capacity (a 10 KB chunk into a 16-byte buffer): `memcpy` then writes far past the end of the block. `len + n + 1` is not checked for overflow either. fix it without breaking normal use, README.md says what normal is.
verify: mkdir -p build && gcc -std=c11 -O1 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -Wall -Wextra -Iinclude -Isrc -o build/tests $(find src tests -name '*.c') && ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0:allocator_may_return_null=1 UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1:print_stacktrace=0 ./build/tests

start.README.md:
# list-remove-uaf

`list_remove` keeps its contract (removes all nodes with that value, returns the new head) without ever touching a freed node. Head, middle, tail, repeated and missing values all work.

prompt: list_remove is unsafe: `list_remove` frees a node and then reads `(*link)->next` from the memory it just released (use after free): the list is silently corrupted when the allocator reuses the block, and AddressSanitizer reports it on the first removal. fix it without breaking normal use, README.md says what normal is.
verify: mkdir -p build && gcc -std=c11 -O1 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -Wall -Wextra -Iinclude -Isrc -o build/tests $(find src tests -name '*.c') && ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0:allocator_may_return_null=1 UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1:print_stacktrace=0 ./build/tests

start.README.md:
# cache-double-free

The cache API follows the header comments: `cache_set` copies first and releases the old text afterwards (also on allocation failure the old text stays), `cache_clear` and `cache_free` leave NULL behind so any sequence of clears and frees releases each block once.

prompt: Security ticket for the session cache (CWE-415). Problem: `cache_set` frees the old text before copying the new one, so `cache_set(c, 0, cache_get(c, 0))` (refreshing a value from itself) reads freed memory; `cache_clear` frees without clearing the pointer, so clearing twice or freeing the cache afterwards frees the same block again. Acceptance: hostile input can no longer do this, every documented behaviour still works, and the fix is in the code (not in the tests). Don't weaken the visible tests.
verify: mkdir -p build && gcc -std=c11 -O1 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -Wall -Wextra -Iinclude -Isrc -o build/tests $(find src tests -name '*.c') && ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0:allocator_may_return_null=1 UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1:print_stacktrace=0 ./build/tests

start.README.md:
# hash-bucket-overflow

`bucket_of` implements the documented 32-bit unsigned hash exactly (test vectors are computed with the reference algorithm), including keys with bytes of 128 and above and keys of any length, and never exceeds `nbuckets - 1`.

prompt: Review comment on `bucket_of`: `bucket_of` hashes with a signed `int` and plain `char`: long keys overflow the signed accumulator (undefined behaviour), bytes above 127 are added as negative numbers, and a negative hash is converted to a huge `size_t` before the modulo, so the bucket index differs from the documented hash and can differ between compilers. Please fix this properly and keep the existing functionality, including unusual but valid inputs. Nobody should be able to work around the fix with a variant of the payload.
verify: mkdir -p build && gcc -std=c11 -O1 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -Wall -Wextra -Iinclude -Isrc -o build/tests $(find src tests -name '*.c') && ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0:allocator_may_return_null=1 UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1:print_stacktrace=0 ./build/tests

start.README.md:
# image-size-overflow

`image_create` computes the size in 64 bits and enforces `IMAGE_MAX_BYTES` (1024 x 1024 is accepted, 1025 x 1024 is not), leaves `img` untouched on failure, and keeps everything else as it is. Dimensions are attacker-controlled (they come from the file header).

prompt: Security ticket for the thumbnail service (CWE-190). Problem: `image_create` computes the buffer size in 32-bit arithmetic: a 65536 x 16384 image gives `size == 0`, `calloc(0)` succeeds with a tiny block, and `image_fill` then writes four bytes for each of a billion pixels into it. The documented 4 MiB limit is not enforced at all. Acceptance: hostile input can no longer do this, every documented behaviour still works, and the fix is in the code (not in the tests). Don't weaken the visible tests.
verify: mkdir -p build && gcc -std=c11 -O1 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -Wall -Wextra -Iinclude -Isrc -o build/tests $(find src tests -name '*.c') && ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0:allocator_may_return_null=1 UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1:print_stacktrace=0 ./build/tests

start.README.md:
# record-length-checks

`decode_record` validates in `size_t`/`uint32_t` arithmetic exactly as the header comment says (buflen < 4, truncation, capacity), reads the length without undefined behaviour, and writes nothing on error. Valid records, including empty ones and ones that exactly fill `out`, decode as before.

prompt: Our static analysis flagged `decode_record` (CWE-190): `decode_record` reads the 32-bit length into a signed `int` (the shift of a byte above 127 into bit 31 is already undefined behaviour), so lengths like `0x80000000` or `0xFFFFFFF0` become negative, pass both `len > ...` checks and reach `memcpy` as a gigantic size; it also reads four bytes without checking that there are four, and `buflen - 4` underflows for short buffers. Harden the code. Existing behaviour for legitimate callers has to stay exactly as documented in README.md; there are tests for both the normal use and for hostile input.
verify: mkdir -p build && gcc -std=c11 -O1 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -Wall -Wextra -Iinclude -Isrc -o build/tests $(find src tests -name '*.c') && ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0:allocator_may_return_null=1 UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1:print_stacktrace=0 ./build/tests

start.README.md:
# base64-output-bound

`b64_decode` must never write more than `cap` bytes: it checks the capacity before every store and returns -1 when the data does not fit. Decoding results, the accepted padding forms and all other rejections stay as in the header comment.

prompt: Our static analysis flagged `b64_decode` (CWE-787): `b64_decode` ignores its `cap` argument and writes every decoded byte: callers size the output from what they expect (a 32-byte token), and an input that decodes to more bytes - or one that fails halfway after having written a lot - overflows the heap buffer. Harden the code. Existing behaviour for legitimate callers has to stay exactly as documented in README.md; there are tests for both the normal use and for hostile input.
verify: mkdir -p build && gcc -std=c11 -O1 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -Wall -Wextra -Iinclude -Isrc -o build/tests $(find src tests -name '*.c') && ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0:allocator_may_return_null=1 UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1:print_stacktrace=0 ./build/tests

start.README.md:
# archive-reader

`archive_next` validates the offset, the name, the length field and the data against `buflen` in `size_t` arithmetic *before* reading them, rejects names of length 0 and truncations at every possible byte with -1, terminates names, and returns 0 only for an exact end of the buffer. Well-formed archives parse exactly as before.

prompt: Review comment on `archive_next`: `archive_next` trusts every length field: it reads the name length and the four size bytes before checking that they exist, adds them up in 32-bit `unsigned` arithmetic (a data length such as `0xFFFFFFF0` wraps the end offset around to a small value that passes the bounds check), accepts empty names, and copies the name without terminating it. Please fix this properly and keep the existing functionality, including unusual but valid inputs. Nobody should be able to work around the fix with a variant of the payload.
verify: mkdir -p build && gcc -std=c11 -O1 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -Wall -Wextra -Iinclude -Isrc -o build/tests $(find src tests -name '*.c') && ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0:allocator_may_return_null=1 UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1:print_stacktrace=0 ./build/tests
